name: Resource-index method
review_status: The decomposition below is derived from a published GESN base: 2604 norms, none with an empty resource list, four resources per norm at the median. The regulatory timeline is drawn from public sources and is pending review by a Russian cost engineer.
description: A Russian norm does not carry a price. It carries quantities: how many man-hours at which grade, how many machine-hours of which plant, how much of which material a unit of the work consumes. The price is assembled afterwards from those quantities and a price book, which is why the same norm serves every region and every year. An estimate that carries rates without the resources behind them has thrown away the part a reviewer checks.

resource_classes.note: Man-hours, normally with the average grade (разряд) of the crew. This is the figure overhead and estimated profit are normed against, so a line without it cannot carry a markup at all.
Sits inside the plant cost and inside payroll at the same time. Counting it once is the point; counting it twice, or in neither place, are the two ways this goes wrong.
Machine-hours per unit of work, by machine type.
Quantities in physical units. A norm may leave a material unpriced and open, to be supplied by the project, in which case the estimate names it.

method_timeline.базисно-индексный: A base-year price multiplied by a conversion index. Long the default, still in wide use for older documentation.
method_timeline.ресурсный: Current prices applied directly to the resource quantities.
method_timeline.ресурсно-индексный: The current method: current prices where the state price system publishes them, indices for the rest. This is what the federal base has been maintained for since the 2022 edition.
